title: Sponson recipe
description: One provider's recipes for the generic http adapter: packages/adapters/recipes/<provider>.yaml. See docs/adr/0020-recipes.md and CONTRIBUTING.md (Adding a recipe).

provider.description: The provider's name: the file's name, and the first half of a line's `recipe: <provider>.<op>`.

title.description: The provider as people write it (Cloudflare).

category.description: The id of a category in docs/coverage.yaml.

verified_on.description: The date the API facts were checked against `docs`.

docs.description: The provider's official pages the recipe was verified against.

api.description: The API block defaults: what `providers.http.<api>: { recipe: <provider> }` means. `base_url` may be left out only for per-account APIs; then every plan sets it. The whole block is left out only by a recipe whose ops are all `action`s sent to the app's own `url` (no credential).

base_url_env.description: The conventional override variable, `<PROVIDER>_API_URL`; the recipe tests point it at the fake cloud.

auth.description: The credential, under the provider's conventional variable name (its CLI's or SDK's).

prefix.description: Literal text sent before the value (`SSWS `, `Api-Key `).

oneOf.description: Several credential headers sent together (Datadog's API and application keys).
HTTP Digest (RFC 7616), answering the server's challenge (MongoDB Atlas API keys).

oauth2_client_credentials.description: A bearer token from the provider's token endpoint (client credentials). A per-account API writes `token_url` and `audience` as paths, resolved against the origin of the plan's `base_url`.

token_url_env.description: The override variable, `<PROVIDER>_TOKEN_URL`; the recipe tests point it at the fake cloud's token endpoint.

oneOf.description: A token the provider's own CLI prints (gcloud, az), run without a shell; literal arguments only.
AWS Signature Version 4, from the AWS CLI's and SDKs' conventional variables.

media_type.description: A versioned JSON media type sent as `Accept` and as the `Content-Type` of bodies (Heroku: `application/vnd.heroku+json; version=3`).

refuse_credential.description: Credentials the API refuses before any request (Stripe's live-mode keys): values starting with one of `prefixes`, unless the variable `unless_env` is 1 or true. A plan cannot override it.

base_url_example.description: For a per-account API (no `api.base_url`): an example base URL, used by the docs' example provider block and the recipe tests. Required then.

detect.description: How `sponson init` detects that a repository uses the provider (names and files only, never a value), and the lines it writes for it. Adding this block is all it takes for init to detect the provider. Left out by a recipe whose provider another file or a first-class adapter already detects.

deps.description: Dependency names in package.json: exact (`stripe`), or a scope or prefix ending in `/` (`@stripe/`).

env.description: Variable names in `.env*` files: exact, or a prefix ending in `*` (`STRIPE_*`). A framework's public prefix (`NEXT_PUBLIC_`, `VITE_`, …) in front matches too.

files.description: Files whose presence is a signal, relative to the repository root.

db_hosts.description: Host suffixes (`.turso.io`) of a database URL in an `.env*` file that point at the provider; only the provider's name leaves the check.

starter.description: The lines `sponson init` writes when it detects the provider (default: one for the first op). A line whose required params are all known is written ready; otherwise it is written commented out, with a `# TODO:` naming where to find each missing param.

preview_url.description: The param that takes the preview's URL, as a whole value: init writes `{ from: <deploy line>.preview_url }` when it writes a deploy target's line.

values.description: Values init writes for these params, typically built from `${ctx.*}` (`preview-${ctx.scope}`).

where.description: Where to find a param's value, by param name (`base_url` for a per-account API's base URL): the `# TODO:` init writes beside it. A param without one gets its description.

assumptions.description: Numbered facts about the API the recipe relies on. Verified ones cite their source.

kind.description: The http op it expands into; the plan line's `op`. `action`: one request sent when its trigger changes (ADR 0022).

covers.description: Ids of docs/coverage.yaml rows this op covers.

http.description: The http.resource, http.list_item or http.action params, without api, vars and destroy. `{ param: <name> }` stands for a param's value; `{<name>}` in a path for its URI-encoded value.

destroy.description: What destroying a scope does with what the op made when the line does not say. Absent: delete it. `keep`: leave it (shared history, such as a release); a line may still write `destroy: delete`. `never`: the provider cannot delete it; it is always left, and `destroy: delete` is refused.

sim.description: How the generic REST sim stands in for the provider in the recipe tests.

id_from.description: The body field a create chooses the id with.

item_query.description: The query parameter that names one object, when the provider keys objects by a value (`url`).

objects.description: Objects to seed, by path (placeholders filled from the examples).

header_fields.description: Request headers a create or update stores as fields (header → field), for an API that takes settings in headers.

suffix_field.description: For a create at `<collection>/{+param}`: the field the sim stores that path suffix in; the POST is an upsert by the chosen id.

collection.description: The collection path (placeholders filled from the examples) a resource lives in, when its create is posted elsewhere. Default: the create's path.

provider.description: A first-class sim (packages/sim/src/routes/<provider>.ts) to run the op against instead of the generic REST sim, for an API the REST sim cannot stand in for (GraphQL). Then `seed`, `present` and `drift` describe the test.

base_path.description: With `provider`: the path under the sim the API's base URL stands for (default `/<provider>`; `/aws/amplify`).

seed.description: With `provider`: that sim's seed (the example values' project, environment or app).

present.description: With `provider`: a JSON pointer into that sim's state that exists once the op applied and is gone after destroy.

drift.description: With `provider`: that sim's drift keys (without the provider prefix) and values that edit a declared field (`changed`) and remove what the op made (`missing`).

console_url.description: The provider console page for what the op made, linked from the PR comment. Only a documented URL pattern: `source` is the provider's page that documents it.

template.description: An `https://` URL with `{<name>}` placeholders: a param, an output, or `id` (the provider id of what the op made); each value is URI-encoded.
